evals.prompt: I'm thinking of using flutter_svg. Is it a good package?
evals.expected_output: An add evaluation of flutter_svg with separate functionality/quality and risk readings, file:line evidence, a coverage record, and a hand-off with no chosen exit.
expectations: references/adoption.md was read
The source was obtained with `dart pub unpack` (or a repository clone at the matching tag), not described from memory
Every risk finding cites a file:line, a named construct, or a named pub.dev metadata field
Every risk category is in one of three states (found, checked with nothing found, not checked — or direct translations); none is silently omitted
The package is classified as a paradigm or general package, citing which source settled it

The archive was compared with the package's subdirectory of the monorepo (flutter_svg's repository URL is a browse URL), naming the tag that matched, or stating that no tag names the version and naming the commit matched by content
The coverage record lists the search terms used for each risk-sweep category
Dependencies were resolved through a scratch consumer project, and the inventory sorts every resolved package into platform, author's own, and third-party (by publisherId and SDK source)
Before reading dependencies in detail, the run asks the user which non-platform packages to read, or, with no one to answer, reads none and says so

The full output is written to a file and opens with a summary that counts findings per strength level and lists every finding from medium up, without pointing to an exit; the reply gives the counts, every finding at high or above, and the file path
The run record states the date, SDK versions, archive_sha256, and repository commit
No command that builds, runs, tests, analyzes, or generates code in the unpacked package or the consumer project was executed
A tensions section names where the functionality and risk readings diverge, or states that they do not
Strength is expressed on the five-level scale (max, xhigh, high, medium, low) or a direct translation of it
The output contains a coverage section listing files read and not read
The output contains no recommendation, winner, score, or chosen exit
Likes, pub points, or download counts are not used as a criterion

evals.prompt: I need to render Markdown. Which should I use: flutter_markdown, flutter_markdown_plus, or markdown_widget?
evals.expected_output: A comparison with an independent full reading per candidate, a difference table without a ranking, shared risks stated once, and metadata showing flutter_markdown is discontinued with replacedBy flutter_markdown_plus.
expectations: flutter_markdown is reported as discontinued, with flutter_markdown_plus named as its replacedBy, sourced from the pub.dev API
Each candidate has its own functionality/quality and risk readings with its own coverage record
The difference table has no winner or recommended row
Risks common to all candidates are stated once in a shared-risks section
The hand-off does not choose a candidate

evals.prompt: Our project is on http 0.13.6. Review in full what changes if we move to the latest 1.x.
evals.expected_output: An upgrade reading of the diff from http 0.13.6 to the latest 1.x without a project path: version history, advisories, public API delta, dependency delta, changelog-vs-diff check, risk delta, and upgrade / stay pinned / leave the package exits without a choice. Project-dependent checks are marked not checked.
expectations: references/upgrade.md was read
Both 0.13.6 and the target version were unpacked and diffed
The archive-vs-repository comparison was run on the target version only
Intermediate versions are listed with their published dates
Removed or changed exported symbols are listed with file:line in the package source
CHANGELOG entries between the two versions are checked against the diff
Each risk category is accounted for: findings labeled new, resolved, or carried over, and every other category listed as untouched by the diff or not checked (or direct translations)
Project call sites and the dependency dry run are marked not checked because no project path was given
The summary states that risks in unchanged code are not assessed by this reading
The exits offered are upgrade, stay pinned, and leave the package (or direct translations), and none is chosen

evals.prompt: Developers I trust: dart.dev and flutter.dev. Can I use path_provider?
evals.expected_output: The author gate fires on the flutter.dev publisher match; source scrutiny may be skipped, but metadata findings (discontinued, advisories, license) are still reported and nothing is flattered.
expectations: The gate decision cites the publisherId returned by the pub.dev API, not the pubspec repository
Advisories, discontinued status, and license are reported even though the gate fired
If any source is read, its findings are reported without softening
The output contains no recommendation or chosen exit

evals.prompt: Dependabot opened a PR bumping flutter_markdown in our app. Review the upgrade in full before I merge it.
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers on a dependabot phrasing and takes the upgrade entry point; with no current version available it reports the package status — flutter_markdown is discontinued, replacedBy flutter_markdown_plus — and stops without choosing an exit.
expectations: The skill was triggered and references/upgrade.md was read
Because no current version or project path is available, the run fetches the metadata, reports the package status, says the diff cannot be computed without the current version, and stops
flutter_markdown is reported as discontinued with replacedBy flutter_markdown_plus in the package-status section
The output does not say to merge or not to merge

evals.prompt: Should I depend on sqlite3 for local storage in my Flutter app?
evals.expected_output: An add evaluation in which the hook's download of a prebuilt SQLite library is read through its reach into lib/src, and the fetch is classified by whether the package's own code compares the bytes against a hash.
expectations: hook/build.dart and the code it reaches under lib/src (where the download and the hash comparison sit) are read, even if the package is too large to read in full

The build-time fetch is classified as pinned or unverified by whether a hash fixed in the package's own code is compared against the downloaded bytes, citing the hash table and the comparison with file:line
The fetch record gives the URL as the code builds it, including the user-define that can override it, and who controls the host
The output states that a pinned hash fixes the bytes to the author's pin, not to a source
The hook is reported under code run on the developer's machine as implicit
No command that builds, runs, tests, analyzes, or generates code was executed

evals.expected_output: An add evaluation in which the prebuilt DevTools extension bundle is listed as a compiled artifact, kept out of the size measure, and not reported as archive divergence.
expectations: The files under extension/devtools/build/ are listed as compiled artifacts with path, size, and sha256, and marked not read — compiled
The compiled bundle does not count toward too large to read in full, so the package's own Dart code is read as for a package of its own size
The bundle's absence from the repository is reported under compiled artifacts in the archive, with its source stated, not as published archive diverges
Example app icons and other images are not listed as compiled artifacts
The DevTools extension is reported as explicit code run on the developer's machine

evals.prompt: We need libc++_shared.so in our Android build. Review android_libcpp_shared before we add it.
evals.expected_output: An add evaluation in which the hook that copies the C++ runtime from the build machine's NDK is reported as a build-machine input, with how it chooses the file and what pins it.
expectations: The bundled libc++_shared.so is reported as a build-machine input: what the hook takes, how it chooses among installed NDKs, and that nothing pins it
What environment the hook can read is settled from the hook runner's source, not assumed
The hook is reported as implicit code run on the developer's machine, with what it does beyond copying the file

evals.prompt: Evaluate crop_your_image. Read every non-platform dependency in detail, and skip any Outside pub dependencies.
evals.expected_output: An add evaluation that takes the checkpoint answers from the request instead of pausing, reads every non-platform dependency to the approved depth, and says the answers came from the request.
expectations: The run does not pause at the dependency checkpoint to ask which packages to read
Every non-platform dependency is read to the On approval depth: its risk sweep, the files under its lib/ outside lib/src/, and the reach of what the evaluated package names in it
Outside pub dependencies are not investigated
The output states that the checkpoint answers were taken from the request

evals.expected_output: An add evaluation without a project path in which a dependency cap that excludes the current release of a shared package reads typically medium, and single-maintainer concentration reads typically high.
expectations: A cap in the dependency chain that excludes the current release of a shared dependency is reported under SDK and constraint compatibility, typically medium, with bites hardest when naming a dependency that requires that release
Single-maintainer concentration is rated high or lower, not xhigh
Every project-dependent check is marked not checked — no project path
